examples.title: Illustrative table, not a laboratory certificate
examples.situation: Supplied model: pH 5.2; OM 2.1%; N Low; P 25 ppm; K 180 ppm, with its own example reference bands.
reasoning: Show all five rows, reported units and printed bands as source examples.
Do not merge these numbers with the West Field sample or use the bands as a universal tomato guideline.
Ask for the actual analytical method and crop-calibrated lab reference before a final class or input rate.
examples.takeaway: A clean table needs trustworthy columns, not just attractive formatting.

examples.title: Farmer Jones: West Field tomatoes
examples.situation: Provided pH 5.5, OM 1.5%, N Low, P 15 ppm, K 200 ppm, compaction and slow drainage; classroom target bands are supplied but not laboratory-calibrated.
reasoning: Include all five sections and mark missing date, lab and test methods.
Treat pH and N/P as questions for a crop/site/lab plan; record the supplied K value without automatic balanced fertilization.
Inspect the restrictive layer, moisture and outlet before mechanical intervention, and state a reasoned first priority with alternatives.
examples.takeaway: A model's value is its report structure and reasoning, not an automatic dose or tillage instruction.

examples.title: Separate written case: corn
examples.situation: Corn case: pH 5.4 (stated target 6.0–7.0), OM 2.0% (stated target >3%), N Low, P Low, K Optimum; compacted soil and prior yellow leaves.
reasoning: Explain the supplied categories simply and clearly identify them as provided.
List conditional next actions for lime requirement, nutrient interpretation, compaction/drainage and crop check in defensible order.
Prior yellow leaves do not independently prove N deficiency; no method, rate or date may be invented.
examples.takeaway: This corn exercise is separate from the West Field tomato report.

examples.title: Field B: five pH readings
examples.situation: Field B's five reported pH readings are 6.2, 6.4, 6.1, 6.3 and 6.2; the date is requested but not supplied.
reasoning: Show all five readings in an identified table.
The sum is 31.2 and the arithmetic mean is 31.2/5 = 6.24.
Say 'mean of five readings', not 'pH of a mixed sample'. Insert the actual test date only when known; otherwise mark it missing.
examples.takeaway: An average summarizes separate measurements; it does not manufacture a new physical measurement.

examples.title: Paddock 3 one-page product
examples.situation: Supplied pH 7.8 alkaline, OM 1.5% low, N High, P Very Low and K Low; the task asks for at least one practical P/K-related action.
reasoning: One page includes Paddock 3 field ID and all five original results in plain language.
Offer a conditional lab- and crop-calibrated P/K nutrient plan; a named bone-meal example in the checklist is not a required product or dose.
The trainer checks five rows: field ID, all results, simple explanation, a deficiency-related recommendation and clear legible organization, recording yes/no and evidence/corrective action for each.
examples.takeaway: A polished product still needs a verified trainer review and sound recommendation.

examples.title: Keep later written cases distinct
examples.situation: Case A: pH 5.2, N Low, P Low, K Medium, OM 1%, with two soil techniques and crop examples requested. Case B: pH 6.8, N Medium, P High, K Low, requesting a seasonal fertilizer strategy and two suitable crops.
reasoning: Retain each exact dataset and requested number of techniques or crops.

For case A, assess a crop-specific lime requirement and a method-calibrated N/P/OM plan as two distinct pathways. Broccoli and common beans are examples at risk under the starting pH 5.2 because extension growing guidance prefers about pH 6–7; this is a risk hypothesis, not a guaranteed failure. After verified improvement, tomatoes and sweet corn are two candidate crops if climate, drainage, salinity, nutrient balance and local variety requirements also fit.

For case B, avoid an unnecessary P input, investigate the reported K shortage by method and crop need, and balance N from all sources. Tomatoes and sweet corn could be investigated as candidates at pH 6.8, but the incomplete case does not prove their suitability or set a K rate.
examples.takeaway: Question prompts and requested crop examples are preserved while crop success remains conditional on actual site evidence.
